When an IT issue crosses teams, who owns the next step?

That question matters when you work with an MSP or external service provider. A ticket can move between a helpdesk, an application owner, and a security team while everyone assumes someone else is following up.

A useful service review starts with three questions:

• Who is responsible for resolving this type of issue?
• Who can approve a change or accept the business impact?
• Who updates the people waiting on a resolution?

Write those answers down for a few common scenarios. Include an unavailable application, a departing employee, and a suspected security incident.

Clear responsibilities make it easier to spot gaps before an urgent situation exposes them. Which handoff would you clarify first?
